svg.text: Grounded in field observations, workshop data, and DORA 2025. Read bottom-up: causes flow upward to effects.
"What's getting in the way of predictable delivery?"
Too much WIP ù Little's Law ù slow flow.
Late deliveries, missing features, quality issues.
Same-day to 6 months. Plans inflated. Missing pieces.
Customer said: "Too much work." Teams on 5+ things.
C7: Late discovery of missing pieces
Find out just before delivery that something is wrong.
More PRs, more bugs, bigger changes, slower reviews.
Root causes (why the delivery system is broken)
C10: No visibility into the value stream
"Understand connections between modules." No e2e view.
C11: Work pushed in, not pulled
"Unclear prioritization." Leadership pushes without capacity check.
More output, same bottlenecks, more chaos.
Why AI makes it worse  local vs. global optimization (Goldratt's Rule #1)
C13: AI produces real local gains
These gains are real  but local, not system-level.
C14: Board/CEO pressure to adopt AI
Career risk to NOT adopt. "We need an AI strategy."
AI is legible to boards; flow management is not.
C15: Local gains mask system problems
More WIP at the bottleneck ù more chaos, not less.
People and culture (why it doesn't get fixed)
C17: Everyone is too busy to fix the system
40+ items/day. No time for improvement work.
C18: Delivery is seen as unfixable
Leaders treat it as weather, not engineering.
Hired agile coaches. Tried Scrum. Didn't stick.
CORE PROBLEM: Nobody manages the flow of work through the system
All root causes trace here. All consultants address symptoms. Addressing THIS = dominant competitive edge.
Above: what the customer experiences. Below: why they don't hire help to fix it.
Risks that prevent buying (why they live with it instead of hiring)
Fought to get budget. Can't waste it.
If it fails, I look bad to leadership.
B4: AI is free, why pay?
Admitting AI isn't working is political.
What they do instead (your real competition)
"I need to fix delivery (the pain is real) BUT I can't risk budget/reputation on something unproven."
What an unrefusable offer must do (Goldratt's value levers)
Show value in 2 weeks, not 3 months.
Quick diagnostic ù surface top bottleneck ù
Tie impact to their metrics (DORA, OKRs).
"What does 1 month of delay cost you?"
Make the cost of inaction concrete.
Your fee is tiny vs. the cost of broken delivery.
Frame against the problem, not against
1. "Leaders see delivery as unfixable complexity"  or is it fixable but not worth the effort? (changes: belief vs. cost/benefit)
2. "Previous improvement attempts failed"  or never tried? (changes: cynical vs. uninformed buyer)
3. "AI is free, why pay a human?"  is admitting AI isn't working politically dangerous? (changes: framing approach)
4. Which buying risks (B1-B5) are the real blockers? (shapes the unrefusable offer)
5. THE QUESTION: "If you had budget for one external person, what problem would you point them at?"
6. What language do they use? Not "flow" or "WIP"  what are their words for these problems?
= UDE painful enough to trigger purchase
Sources: DORA 2025 (n=4,916), Faros AI Productivity Paradox, customer mapping sessions, qualitative field observations.
